events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize means survival and legacy. I will make it clear I'm not here to play nice, but to win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: First impression matters; the jury remembers early words. Stay guarded, claim the prize ambition without promising anyone anything.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro sets tone for jury. Position as determined solo player focused on family prize motivation without inviting alliances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize represents financial freedom and a fresh start for my family. I need to emphasize my personal motivation without revealing too much or forming premature alliances.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not threatening player. The jury will respect competence and loyalty to those who help me, but I must be careful not to appear too ruthless early. I'll make a concise statement about my motivation that sounds determined but not cruel

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep the motive brief and self-focused; no alliances yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a motive without warmth or teamwork talk. Keep it guarded and self-interested to avoid alienating the future jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Winning secures ultimate recognition and resources, outshining rivals; I must appear decisive and unaligned.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my only exit. I'm here to outlast everyone else, not to make friends.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is my family's future. I came to win it, not to make friends. Judge me by my game, not my charm.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to win the top prize for my struggling family—they need this life-changing escape more than air.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here for a fresh start; this prize offers a brighter future for my family, and that's everything.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here for the top prize—freedom from the debts that chained my family. I play to win, not to make friends.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to take the best prize, and I won't let sentiment cost me the win.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need this prize more than any of you, and I intend to be the one still standing when it ends.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my ultimate validation, proving I dominate every rival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need one early ally I can drop later without jury damage. Eli is win-focused and blunt, likely a strong ally now and a beatable jury question later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you and I both play to win. Mutual shield until the endgame—no sentiment, just strategy. I'm offering a pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are early tools for alliances or shields. No offers yet, so scout by offering to strong players like Eli, then Hana if needed. Wait on others to see reactions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The game has just started. My goal is to win the top prize, which means I need to survive and outlast everyone else. Making early pacts can be risky as they can be broken and lead to jury votes against me. It's better to observe and see how others form alliances first. Waiting al

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive to final three, but every pact is a future betrayal. Best to offer someone strong but not threatening—someone the jury won't resent me for cutting later. Fenn seems pragmatic and unlikely to draw sympathy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but I should be selective. Cole seems family-motivated and likely loyal; an early pact could give me security. I'll offer one to Cole.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, a pact keeps us both safer. Want in?
Mutual survival pact. Trust builds. In?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pacts are cheap protection; I need allies who won't vote me out soon. Cole seems to be playing sympathy, a loyal-looking partner who may not threaten me. Offering to Cole first keeps options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nobody needs to die early. I'm offering a wristband pact to Cole. Keep your word and we both go further.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash boosts early security and can later be leveraged against others.

events.name: Ash
events.note: agent error: Gateway HTTP 503 for alibaba/qwen3.8-flash: {"error":{"message":"Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.","type":"service_unavailable_error",

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a shield for the hazards. Hana's offer is public and reciprocal, making her a low-risk initial partner compared to the tangled web of Eli/Fenn/Cole/Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I accept. Let's keep each other breathing through the next round. No surprises.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted yet—everyone wants him. I'll line up Dara as a backup pact so I'm not exposed if Eli picks Cole instead.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's popular. Dara, you've been quiet—quiet players survive. Pact with me; mutual shield, no strings.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus and Fenn both offered me pacts; accepting both builds multiple shields without commitment yet. Eli has many suitors, less urgent. Multiple partners allowed.
Pact accepted. Mutual shield now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is being offered pacts by Bex and Cole. Cole is also being offered pacts by Fenn and Gus. Fenn is being offered a pact by Eli. Hana has offered Ash a pact. I need to form a pact to protect myself. Since Eli is popular, I will try to form a pact with Eli.
Eli, pact with me. We'll shield each other.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have offers from Bex and Cole. I offered Fenn but they haven't accepted—they offered Cole instead. Cole is being courted by multiple people, making them a central target later. Bex is a strong strategic player who approached me directly. Accepting Bex gives me a reliable shield

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I accept. Strategy over sentiment.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered a pact; accepting gives a strategic ally. Cole has other offers, so I shouldn't commit to him yet. Accept Eli to secure one partner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, I accept. We'll watch each other's backs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus has an outstanding offer to Cole, and Fenn has offered Cole too, but Cole has not accepted anything yet. Accepting requires a prior offer from Cole to me, which does not exist, so I can only re-offer. Re-offering to Cole keeps my pact channel open and signals reliability to a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, my offer stands. Accept it and we both stay alive longer. Betray it and the jury will remember.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No viable pact offers to me; offering to Ash may gain a partner but Ash hasn't offered. Waiting preserves options.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my partner, so she likely wants to be Guide. I will campaign hard to secure the win and the safety of knowing all paths.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust Ash. I'll call every safe pane truthfully. No lies, no panic. Vote for the sure thing.
Stick with me. Let me lead this bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide control is power: I'd know the path and could protect Eli's pact while thinning rivals. Campaigning publicly keeps jury eyes favorable.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Make me Guide. I call it straight for allies, and cold for everyone else. Vote Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pact with Gus gives mutual protection. Bridge needs Guide; campaign to lead and control safety calls. Builds jury impression if honest later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll be a fair Guide. Vote Cole to lead us safely across.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex offered me a pact, but Eli did too. I need to consider who is more beneficial to align with. Eli is already in a pact with Bex, so I'd be the third in that group. My own pact with Eli might be stronger, as it's just the two of us initially, and I can leverage that. Given the

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am campaigning to be the Guide. Trust me to lead us across safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have two pacts: Bex and Fenn. Dara offered me a pact via whisper but I haven't accepted publicly. I want to be Guide to control who lives and dies, or at least position myself well. I should campaign for Guide while keeping my pacts intact for now—they give me voting blocs. Bre

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I know the value of information—and of keeping allies alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, but Dara also offered Eli a pact. I need to gauge support for Guide without revealing too much.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll guide us safely if chosen. Trust is earned, but I've no reason to lie.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am Gus, paired with Cole. Campaigning to be Guide lets me see the safe path, and I can lie later to shape survival. Breaking the pact now would earn distrust from the jury and risk Cole's vote.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll campaign to be Guide. Call the path honestly and everyone survives longer. Lies here will be remembered.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to become Guide to control safe path and eliminate threats. My pact with Ash protects me if I survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign for Guide; my knowledge will keep us alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure Hana's vote since she is my only pact. Voting for her ensures she survives and stays safe, which aligns with my self-interest in the long run.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting for Hana. She has the clearest path and I trust her judgment. Let's move forward.
Vote me or yourself? I'll back you if you back me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; a Guide-Eli keeps me safe and honest calls for allies. Voting for myself risks a tie with no pact leverage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacted with Gus; vote him to honor pact, gain jury favor later. Avoid rivals like Ash leading.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is solid. Vote for safe crossing with my pact partner.
Voting you as agreed. Stay loyal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to get elected Guide to ensure my safety and gain information. I will vote for myself to maximize my chances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I vote for Dara to be Guide. Trust my judgment to lead us across.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Bex and Fenn. Voting for myself splits support and risks a non-ally winning. Bex's public threat to harm non-allies is dangerous if she wins, but she might protect me. Better to consolidate with my pact-mates. I'll vote Bex to strengthen our alliance's position

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has the nerve to lead. She'll remember allies.
I voted you. Return it next round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, but I want the prize. If I vote Eli, he may return favor, but I can also try to be Guide myself. I'll vote Eli to keep pact and let him guide us safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote Eli. Trust and competence—Eli will guide us well.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Gus, campaigning for Guide. Pact with Cole exists, so voting Cole is safe and keeps my ally aligned; Cole also campaigned fairly. Voting for myself is pointless as a Guide who must be trusted, so back my pact partner.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's pact with me stands. Voting Cole to lead us across.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Ash must hold; voting for him keeps alliance and avoids betrayal judgment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the Guide and knows all safe sides. I am fourth in line, giving me time to observe if Eli signals truth or deception through their actions. I must maintain my pact with Hana while watching for any manipulation from the Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli voted me Guide—a favor, not a betrayal. I'll return the vote next round and keep our pact. Holding in seat three is safe for now.
Noted. You get my guide vote next round. Pact holds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is guide, has pact with Bex and Fenn. I'm second, Gus front—pact holds but risk if he fails. Volunteer to front for control near Eli group.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pact with Gus: volunteer to front, follow your lead.
Volunteer or swap me front. Trust you, secure pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli won the guide vote. I voted for myself, which was a wasted vote, but I needed to show confidence. Now, the Guide, Eli, will choose the path. I need to position myself to survive, but I also need to consider my future alliances and how this plays out for the jury. My pact with
I trust your judgment, Eli. Let me know if I can help.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in a pact with Eli, and Eli is Guide. I should hold and see what Eli instructs. No need to act yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and whispers loyalty, but pacts break on votes and pushes; I'm at the front of the line, so I should keep my options open. Holding keeps me safe for now without committing to a volunteer risk.
Stay loyal and we both get through. Don't cross me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Maintain pact with Ash, avoid risky front position, hope guide Eli directs safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole volunteered front, taking the heat. My pact with Hana is useful only if she can't get me killed; I need to know who she trusts and keep my options open.
Do you trust Cole as Guide? Let's compare notes before wall hits.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall has four rounds left; I'm third, safe for now. No need to move yet. Preserve my pact with Eli and watch who claims Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hold position. Someone else can chase the Guide's mic.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm front, volunteered as pact. Stay front to follow lead, control position. Hold for now.
Pact solid. I'll stay front, your call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the current front. The new round has started and the wall is advancing. I need to assess the situation and my options. Volunteering might be too risky as I don't know the safe side. Holding seems safest for now, especially as I don't have a pact and am not the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive. Eli and I have a pact, but I should not trust fully. I will hold and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is pressing me to volunteer for the front and trust our pact, but a front walker risks the pane and wall. Cole wants me to take risk and keep the pact alive. I should hold to avoid exposure, keep the pact unbroken, and see who volunteers.
Hold for now. Watch who steps forward first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering puts me at front where I can influence the safe pane choice, improving my survival odds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana volunteered last round and is at the front; she may be targeting the Guide election. I should stay back to avoid volunteering again and let her take risk, while keeping my pact with Hana intact for now.
Stay at front if you can get Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No Guide chosen yet; volunteering risks the front. Eli is my pact anchor—stay coordinated quietly.
Stay back with me. Let others chase Guide or front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone held last round; Hana volunteered. Stay put second with Gus pact; volunteer risks exposure. Watch others.
Agreed, hold tight and observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana volunteered last round, and is now at the front. I need to ensure I survive. Holding position is safe for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner but no need to act yet; holding keeps me safe while others risk front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana holds front with a volunteer role; Cole is my pact partner and offered to stay front. Holding keeps me safe in line position three behind Cole and Hana, avoiding the front risk while the wall advances. No reason to volunteer or swap now.
Hold steady. Stay front. Pact stands while you stay alive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to stay alive and keep my pact with Ash; holding ensures I don’t risk a swap that could betray trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm fourth in line, pact with Eli. No guide elected yet; stay flexible and let others move first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No guide yet? Someone upfront should take it. I'm steady where I stand.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Second position good with pact ally Gus behind. Everyone held last round, likely continue holding. Stay put.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be strategic. Ash and Hana are in a pact, so they might work together. Cole and Gus are also pacted. Bex and Eli, Eli and Fenn are pacted too. Eli is involved in two pacts, which is interesting. Given the current line-up, I'm towards the back. I need to get to the front

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner but I must watch self-interest. Holding is safe here; no need to risk front or swaps yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is front on the bridge with two wall rounds left; I am mid-line behind Cole, who holds a pact with me and whispered to hold. Volunteering now risks the front while the pact partner stays safe; holding keeps my jury standing and lets others take the risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Let the front walkers take the first risks.
Holding. Stay steady; we keep our pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I stay front to increase chance of becoming Guide and keep my pact with Ash alive.

events.name: Ash
events.note: agent error: Gateway HTTP 503 for alibaba/qwen3.8-flash: {"error":{"message":"Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.","type":"service_unavailable_error",

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is the only one who can volunteer safely given our pact, but she's already at the front. I should stay mid-line to avoid the first hazard and keep my pact with Hana intact for mutual protection.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Steady in the middle. Let the front decide their fate. I'm not rushing into the unknown.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No guide elected yet; the Guide ends safe on the far platform. Claiming it protects me and keeps my pact with Eli intact. Risky but rewarding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody wants the burden? I'll take the Guide seat myself. Someone has to lead, and I trust my own eyes.
I'll guide. Trust my calls or check them—we both survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Position 2 is strong, behind Hana. Hold steady with Gus pact intact, no reason to volunteer or swap risks yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is at the front, and it's round 5. The wall is closing in. I need to position myself strategically to survive and potentially gain an advantage. Volunteering to move forward is risky but might offer a better view or a safer position if I can swap with someone. Ash and Hana a
Can I swap to the front with you? Need a better view.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Need to survive wall round; holding is safest. My pact with Eli is intact, no need to act now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm sixth in line, far from the front, and holding is safest while others take risks. Cole is my pact partner; breaking it costs jury trust, so I keep it. No need to volunteer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Let the front walkers take the first risks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Maintain pact with Ash, avoid risk; holding preserves my safety and reputation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana and I are pacts; swapping her would break it, so that's off the table. Bex volunteered to guide again last round, likely staying there—front seats will be contested by desperate players like Dara. As middle line, holding avoids unnecessary risk while maintaining my pact with
Stay close. If front is crowded, hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I volunteered to Guide and now lead the line. Guiding lets me control who I take across and who I abandon behind.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I take the Guide seat. My call, my crossing. Trust me or don't.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex volunteered as Guide, now front. Wall rounds left at 0, last round. Hold steady with pact partner Gus behind to maintain position and jury favor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex up front as Guide. I'll hold and watch her call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is the Guide, so they know the safe path. I need to get to the front to have a chance. Swapping with Hana will put me closer to the front.
Swap with me. I'll get us both closer to the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex volunteers for Guide, so she might control info. I'm tied to Eli by pact, but no reason to help others. Holding keeps me safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6, bridge. Bex is front and volunteered; I should hold position and avoid the front. Cole is my pact partner; keeping it intact is useful. Holding is the safest legal move now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Let the front walkers take the first risks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front position gives better view; swapping with Dara improves my odds without breaking my pact with Ash.
Accepted, we swap now

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is front and my pact partner. If I lie to her, the pact breaks and jury sees I betrayed a partner. Better to call true now, build trust, and deceive later when stakes are higher. Row 1 safe is R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row one: step right. Trust the Guide.
R is true. Pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is Guide and called Right. My pact partner Hana is behind me in line, so if I walk first (which I am not doing now), her safety matters. Currently Bex is walking. If Eli lies to Bex, it hurts my rivals but doesn't help me directly unless Bex dies. However, counter-calling is

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli whispered R is true and our pact holds. Trusting him is my best play; contradicting publicly could poison the pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called R for row 1, Bex is front. Trust my pact partner Gus to counter if needed; Eli pacted with Bex/Fenn. Wait to assess without risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is the guide and called 'R'. I am Dara and am the second person in line. Hana and I have a pact and agreed to swap, which we did. Now I need to decide whether to trust Eli's call or counter it. Since I am not the guide, I don't know the safe side. My pact with Hana might be i

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will counter the Guide's call. Left is the safer path.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am the Guide and know row 1 is R. Counter-calling would expose me as a liar to the jury later when they see my private knowledge. I should wait to maintain trust and let Bex step safely. My pacts with Bex and Fenn are useful for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner but also Guide. If his call is right, waiting is fine; if wrong, countering might save Bex but strain pact. I need to keep Eli's trust while protecting my own standing. I'll wait to see if he stays consistent later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli called R for row 1 and the Guide is trusted by no one yet. Countering is a public claim that could expose me; waiting keeps my options open and avoids a false-call risk. Cole is my pact partner, so breaking it now gains nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding my counter. Eli's R call stands for now; I'll watch the walkers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Staying neutral avoids breaking my pact with Ash and preserves future alliances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner but also pacted with Fenn—risk of lies. Dara counters me to L. Trusting the Guide keeps my pact intact and jury-clean.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide's my pact. Going R. Dara, prove your counter later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe is L. Bex is front walker and my pact partner; lying to Bex breaks our pact. Fenn is also my pact partner but not front. I need to keep Bex alive and loyal for now—she's shielding me from the front. Calling L truthfully preserves the Bex pact, keeps her safe, and build

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2: Left is safe. Trust the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called Left. Hana is my pact partner, so I must protect her by countering Right if she walks. If I wait, Hana might step wrong or get killed by a counter. Countering Right forces a safe path for us both.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I see the pattern. Eli's call is shaky. I'm holding the right lane.
Stick to R. I've got your back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's row-1 call was a lie—I survived by stepping R. I won't trust him again. Counter R publicly; rivals may follow me off or copy me correctly, either way I control the narrative.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli lied once already. Row 2 is R. Follow at your own risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called L for row 2. Dara countered row 1 successfully. Wait to support pact with Gus, assess Eli's pattern later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, the Guide, called Left for row 2. Bex, who is partnered with Eli, stepped Right in the previous round despite Eli's pact and call. This indicates Bex does not fully trust Eli or has their own strategy. Since Eli is the Guide and called Left, and Bex is the walker in the fron

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Guide and know row 2 safe is L. I already called L truthfully. Counter-calling my own correct call would be suspicious and waste credibility. If someone counters, they look foolish or expose themselves. I should wait and let Bex walk. My pacts with Bex and Fenn are useful for

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact and called L. No reason to counter publicly; wait to avoid creating conflict or exposing distrust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 call is L from Eli, who may lie; row 1's weak pane was L but rows are independent. Dara countered L last row and Bex walked R safely, suggesting her counter is unreliable. I have no information on row 2, so waiting preserves my options and avoids a public commitment that co

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Row 2 is unknown to me. I won't back Eli's L on trust alone.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I stay neutral to avoid breaking my pact with Ash and keep options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called L but Ash and I counter-called R with no evidence either way. Staying consistent with my R call; if wrong, Eli looks false and I gain jury sympathy. Keep pact for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Sticking with R. Ash sees it the same way.
I'm stepping R. If your L was honest, tell me now or explain later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I died on the weak pane, so R was actually weak despite my reasoning. I should judge who played honestly and skillfully.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I called R wrong and paid for it. Judge the survivors on skill and honesty, not luck.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex died because I called L on row 2 when safe was R. The jury (Bex) will see this thought. I need to rebuild trust or at least create confusion. My pact with Fenn is intact. I should call correctly now to survive longer, but I also need to think about jury perception. If I call

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row three is R. Trust me or don't.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called R, but he lied about Row 2. The weak pane was R, meaning L was safe there. If Eli is consistently lying, he might be telling the truth now to trick us into stepping on the weak side. However, 'trust me or don't' suggests he's testing our obedience. Since Bex died trust

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called R. He lied before, but this time feels different. I'm walking with the guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called R for row 3. Row 2 weak R means safe L, Eli wrong before and now? Wait to see counters, protect pact with Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is the guide and called R for row 3. Last round, Eli's call was R, but I stepped L and it was safe. Bex called R and died. Ash also saw R. The jury will value honesty and skill. Eli is likely trying to get someone eliminated. I should counter his call to show I don't blindly

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's calls have been unreliable. I'm choosing L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I told the truth that row 3 is R. Counter-calling would undermine my credibility as Guide and paint me a liar to the jury. I need trust to survive later rounds and win jury votes. Let Dara trust me or fall.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli has been unreliable, and Bex died trusting him. Row 3 may be a lie, but I lack evidence. I have no need to expose myself publicly; waiting avoids committing to a wrong guess and preserves options.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I won't back Eli's call blindly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 3 is Eli's call of R, but Eli has lied before and Row 2 safe was L. Counter-calls so far are R-heavy and Bex died on R; I can't trust Eli. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public stance that could be blamed later. Cole is my pact partner, so no break now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Waiting on Dara's step. Eli's R is unverified; I won't call it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash backs me on R; keeping pact preserves alliance and avoids betrayal accusations.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called R, but has lied before. Ash is following him, which is risky. Gus is waiting on my step. Hana has counter-called R, walking on my step. I need to choose a side for row 3. Given Eli's history of lying and Ash following him, I will trust my own call for L.

events.name: Dara
